channel.title: Shop Talk from Creedy Solutions
channel.description: A one-person app shop, out loud. Chris Reedy, 35 years of electric guitar and a former worship leader, talks through the apps he builds (DrumClock, Chartless) with Nova, a synthetic co-host who asks the hard ones. How the apps work, what they get wrong, and what they're for. Eight minutes an episode, every other Tuesday.
channel.itunes:author: Chris Reedy

item.title: 1. Your drummer is the click: DrumClock, for bands with no in-ears and players who hate the click
item.description:
Most bands play to a click. Plenty of bands can't, and some players won't. DrumClock puts a phone by the kit, listens to the drummer, and sends MIDI clock and tap tempo to the keys rig, pedals and DAW. Chris answers the skeptic questions: how a phone pulls a tempo out of a live kit, what happens on a break, the stick count-off, the Sunday Keys tap-tempo problem, set-list presets, and what it gets wrong.

item.title: 2. No song left behind: Chartless, live chord charts for the Sunday set you got on Thursday
item.description:
The set lands Thursday night, two songs you've never played, one chart in the wrong key. Chartless listens to the actual recording, in a browser tab or through the mic, and shows the chords live, in key, on the beat, then reads the whole song into bars. Chris answers the skeptic questions: why chord apps are a little wrong and how Simple mode fixes that for worship and folk, why there is no AI in the app, the other four tabs, why a guitar with every needle dead center still sounds sour and what Magical tuning does about it, where it runs, and who it is not for.

item.title: 3. Learn the song, not the chart: Practicing, capo positions and alternate tunings for worship players
item.description:
Not the Thursday emergency this time. The craft side: sitting with a song, looping the bridge at sixty, trying two or three capo spots with the chords running, charts in drop D and DADGAD, and why the number system does more for a volunteer player than anything else.

item.title: 4. A practice room students will actually open: Chartless for guitar, uke, piano and bass teachers
item.description:
The lesson ends and the paper doesn't make any sound. Build the progression in the lesson, loop it over a pad, send it home on the phone. One chart for nine instruments, Nashville numbers for beginners, chords from the YouTube lesson, PDFs for the folder, and no account or ads on a kid's phone.

item.title: 5. Done tapping: DrumClock for the guitar player with a delay pedal and no click
item.description:
Chris has stomped a tap tempo button between parts for twenty years. Now the iPad sits on his music stand where he can watch the ring lock, a mic on a boom by the kick runs into a Scarlett, and the Scarlett's MIDI out runs into his pedals, so the delay lands on the drummer's time from the first downbeat. Count-off, the plus or minus eight BPM anchor, set lists on a foot switch, what it gets wrong, and what it costs.
